pr.title: Introduce PlaceContext::may_observe_address.
pr.description:
A small utility method to avoid open-coding the logic in several MIR opts.

processing.reason: No source-grounded counterexample can be validated for this PR. The only context newly added to `excluded_locals` compared with the old open-coded predicate is `NonMutatingUseContext::FakeBorrow` (the other contexts are already covered by `is_borrow`, `is_address_of`, or `is_drop`). A MIR `FakeBorrow` is a borrow-checker artifact with no runtime observation: `CleanupPostBorrowck` turns fake-borrow assignments (and `FakeRead`s) into `Nop` before runtime MIR lowering, and SROA/DataflowConstProp run later on runtime MIR. Thus both the old and new `excluded_locals` see the same fake-borrow-free bodies for these passes, and in any case a fake borrow never exposes a pointer or address to program code. Consequently, omitting `FakeBorrow` from the exclusion set cannot change the observable result of a defined Rust source program through SROA or DataflowConstProp. Constructing a differing pair would require modeling a real shared/raw borrow or a genuine address observer, which is a different `PlaceContext` transformation not justified by this PR's exact delta. The PR itself is a utility refactor, has no confirmed miscompilation, and adds no regression test; the frozen "testStrategy" explicitly claims no execution or reproduction.

analysis.summary: This PR introduces `PlaceContext::may_observe_address` and replaces the open-coded exclusion predicate in `value_analysis::excluded_locals`. The behavioral delta relevant to SROA and DataflowConstProp is that `FakeBorrow` now counts as address-observing: previously a non-indirect place used in `NonMutatingUseContext::FakeBorrow` was not excluded from value tracking, so SROA/DataflowConstProp could treat such a local as eligible for scalar replacement or constant/value propagation. The PR description frames this as a utility refactor, not a confirmed bug fix, but the shared analysis input changes for both passes.
analysis.originalLogic: `excluded_locals(body)` collects locals whose address may be observed. Before this PR, its `visit_place` used the open-coded predicate `context.is_borrow() || context.is_address_of() || context.is_drop() || context == PlaceContext::MutatingUse(MutatingUseContext::AsmOutput)`, guarded by `!place.is_indirect()`. That union did not include `NonMutatingUseContext::FakeBorrow`. SROA consumes `excluded_locals` directly, and DataflowConstProp via `Map::new`, so both passes treated fake-borrowed locals as address-unobserved.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical pre-PR transformation is: when SROA scalarizes an aggregate local, or DataflowConstProp tracks/propagates values for a local, a local that appears in a non-indirect `FakeBorrow` place context is still treated as eligible because `excluded_locals` omits `FakeBorrow`. The correction is to use `context.may_observe_address()`, whose explicit members include `NonMutatingUseContext::FakeBorrow`, so such a local is inserted into the exclusion set and is not scalarized/value-tracked by these passes.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing non-indirect places used in `PlaceContext::NonMutatingUse(NonMutatingUseContext::FakeBorrow)`, especially locals/aggregates that are otherwise candidates for SROA or for DataflowConstProp's value analysis. Fake borrows are emitted by MIR lowering (for example around match scrutinees/guards and other places whose contents must remain stable while a borrow-like observation is live). The exclusion only applies when `!place.is_indirect()`.
analysis.trigger: A local has at least one non-indirect place use in a `FakeBorrow` context, and the body is processed by SROA or DataflowConstProp, both of which derive their tracked-place exclusion set from `excluded_locals`.
preconditions: The place is non-indirect: the old and new conditions both include `&& !place.is_indirect()`.
The body contains a `PlaceContext::NonMutatingUse(NonMutatingUseContext::FakeBorrow)` use of the local.
The consuming pass uses `excluded_locals`: SROA directly, DataflowConstProp through `value_analysis::Map::new`.
The local would otherwise be eligible for the pass's transformation (e.g. an aggregate candidate for SROA, or a tracked place for DataflowConstProp).
pitfalls: Do not claim the PR was reported as a confirmed bug fix: the title/description only say it introduces a utility method to avoid open-coding across MIR opts.
Do not broaden the change to indirect places; `!place.is_indirect()` remains part of the predicate.
Do not conflate `FakeBorrow` with `SharedBorrow`/`RawBorrow`; `may_observe_address` groups them for exclusion, but `FakeBorrow` is the newly added context relative to the old open-coded union.

The `ssa.rs` edit moves `borrowed_locals.insert` to the `may_observe_address` check; treat that as a separate shared SSA-helper change, not as evidence of a concrete SROA or DataflowConstProp contract change.
Do not infer execution or reproduction: no compiler was built in this review.
analysis.testStrategy: Build two MIR-level test cases that differ only in whether the candidate local has a `FakeBorrow` place use: one with a non-indirect `NonMutatingUseContext::FakeBorrow` and one without it. Run SROA/DataflowConstProp and assert that the fake-borrowed local is present in `excluded_locals` and therefore not scalar-replaced/value-tracked, while the otherwise identical local without the fake borrow remains eligible. Add a focused unit test that `PlaceContext::NonMutatingUse(NonMutatingUseContext::FakeBorrow).may_observe_address()` is true, and a MIR visitor test that `excluded_locals` inserts a local when visiting a non-indirect fake-borrow place. This is a proposed testing strategy only; no execution/reproduction is claimed.
evidence: A small utility method to avoid open-coding the logic in several MIR opts.
